messages:
Carla: Quick heads-up — planning to cut release/1.13 today at 18:00 PT. Please get any backport requests in by 15:00 PT so we can triage before the freeze.
Ben: Copy, will submit the runtime flag bump PR now. linking: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821
Alice: I can take the changelog bump. If your PR has user-visible behavior, add a one-line blurb under "Unreleased" and tag me.
Dan: Question — do we allow backports for perf-only changes (no API) after cutoff if they have a perf test?
Carla: Short answer: prefer pushing to next minor. Exception for critical perf regressions with test coverage + perf run. Mark with label `backport/approve` and add justification in PR body.
Ben: Noted. My PR has a tiny behavior doc change though — will add changelog blurb and ping Alice.
Alice: got it. Also, reminder: any cherry-pick must include the original PR number in the title and the test run link in the description. Helps release notes automation.
Dan: If someone needs a branch created early for local testing, can we create release/1.13 now or wait until cut time?
ReleaseBot: automated: creating branch release/1.13 from origin/main at commit abc123def (merge-driver: on).
Carla: ReleaseBot already made it — perfect. Folks: do not push straight to release/* without PR. Use `git checkout -b fix/123-release-1.13` and open the PR targetting release/1.13.
Ben: command for folks —
```
# create local branch from remote release (if you need to test locally before PR)
git fetch origin
git checkout -b fix/4821-release-1.13 origin/release/1.13
# after commits
git push origin fix/4821-release-1.13
```
Alice: Small process note — label convention: `release/1.13` for targeting branch, `backport/approved` after patch lead OKs. I will watch for the label and update changelog.
Dan: Ran into a conflict when cherry-picking 4702 -> release/1.13. Is it okay to resolve and push the backport PR with the conflict resolution?
Carla: Yes, resolve conflicts locally, run unit tests, and add a short note in the PR about conflict rationale (e.g., changed function signature). If it's risky, flag `release-urgent` and we'll review faster.
Ben: FYI: my runtime flag PR added a migration step. Does that block backport?
Carla: Migrations are tricky. If migration is backward-compatible and small, we can include. If it changes DB schema, we should schedule for the next minor unless ops signs off. Please add the migration checklist in the PR.
Alice: I'll do a pre-changelog pass at 16:30 PT and assemble the release section. If you want a specific phrasing, ping me before then.
Dan: tagging @Carla for final signoff after triage.
Carla: Will triage at 15:00 PT. Quick checklist for folks: 1) PR targets release/1.13 or main (with backport request), 2) tests passing on CI, 3) changelog blurb if user-visible, 4) include original PR number in title, 5) add `backport/approved` label once approved.
Ben: :thumbsup: I'll add the labels and bump the PR description.
ReleaseBot: notice: scheduled cut at 18:00 PT. Creating protected branch rule to prevent direct pushes.
Alice: Thanks — reminder to attach any cherry-pick verification logs to the PR (`/artifacts` link), saves us time during the handoff.
Dan: Ok, will aim to get my backport PR up by 13:30 PT for extra review time.
Carla: Thanks everyone. If anything blocks, drop it here and I'll escalate to oncall.
Ben: One last ask — can we have a short note in the release Slack channel after cut with the commit range? Automate if possible.
ReleaseBot: done: post-cut summary will include commit range, changelog snapshot, and list of backported PRs.
Alice: Perfect. See y'all at triage. :rocket:
